reviews.text: Careful, careful. I won't say more.

The truth is, my experience at this hospital has been excellent, both in terms of medical professionalism and personal care. Antonio handled Pepa's case, and I have absolutely no complaints. The dog arrived with a very complex condition and very ill, and he has been completely dedicated to her treatment and recovery. At the moment, we are doing very well and she is nearing the end of her recovery. Many thanks to Antonio and the entire team ❤️‍🩹

Edited after a few weeks: I am still delighted. The treatment from the entire team is wonderful, and they seem to have a great rapport, which speaks volumes. The reception staff are lovely. I am thrilled with the hospital; Pepa is now fully recovered, and Antonio, thanks to his keen clinical eye, has also noticed that she is hypothyroid, which has explained many things.
I've had incredibly bad luck, and my cat Samuela has also fallen ill. Antonio discovered that she is diabetic, and we have started treatment. I'm sure the disease will be under control soon. But the entire experience during both animals' clinical procedures has been incredible, and I have absolutely no complaints.

And you can tell it's a hospital; they have all the necessary materials and resources on hand, the professionals are top-notch, and honestly, their prices are no different from the local clinics I know.

Thank you all 💖
We went to the emergency room with my dog ​​and they treated us wonderfully.

This center is highly recommended. I arrived two years ago with my son Enzo, who was very, very ill, and Iris never wavered. She fought alongside us for him, caring for him and never giving up. We will always be grateful for your work.

Two years later, it was no longer possible, and amidst this grief we are going through, we also want to thank Fernando for the tact and empathy with which he treated Enzo and us. We will always remember and recommend you.

This is my go-to veterinary clinic. The team is made up of amazing professionals. There's no better place to care for my dogs, Uke and Kata. Uke had surgery at this hospital, and the care they gave us was incredible. Thank you all for being so exceptional.

The treatment I received was appalling. I took my dog ​​in because she had vomited blood, as a veterinarian at this hospital had advised. The receptionist, besides being unpleasant, took my information without any urgency. After several questions, I reiterated that she was an urgent referral and asked if we could fill out her file later, which she refused. I insisted again, and she reluctantly notified the veterinarian without any urgency.
My dog ​​was admitted, and I received contradictory information; each person, each veterinarian, told me something different. There was a complete lack of coordination and a brutal lack of consistency.
They only allow you to see her for 10 minutes in 24 hours. She was kept in a cage for 24 hours straight. During visiting hours, dogs were brought up with wet patches on their bodies, which I suppose is because they get wet from the water bowl since they have so little space to move around. The empathy of most of the staff was appalling. They kept asking me why I was so upset, saying they didn't understand (I was just crying because I didn't know what was wrong with her; no one was telling me anything, only that she was stable).
I won't be going back, and I won't recommend it to anyone. I live in the neighborhood, and I know many people who are unhappy with this place but don't leave reviews because they're too old to know how.
The only person who treated me like a human being was David. He took my dog ​​up to the vet during visiting hours and understood my reason for taking her home so she could eat and start getting better.

A perfect 10 experience. The care has been wonderful from the first email until Luna's discharge from the hospital. We are thrilled with the operation and her recovery; we were kept informed and the guidelines were explained to us with great care and patience. Thank you so much, from the bottom of our hearts 💜 …
Making an appointment here is useless; you always, and I mean ALWAYS, have to wait at least an hour, even if you arrive on time. At least they don't charge for emergency service.
Excellent service and outstanding professionals. 100% recommended.

Very worrying care, disorganization, and significant difficulties accessing diagnostic tests.

Our dog, Shanna, eight and a half years old, was seen at this hospital after presenting with a cervical mass, episodes of respiratory distress, and a hypothermia of 35°C.

During the appointment on October 1st, we had to ask the veterinarian, Antonio, THREE TIMES to take her temperature again, despite knowing about the hypothermia episode earlier that morning. When he finally agreed, he had to search for a thermometer in various drawers and examination rooms.

We found it alarming that we had to insist so much on a check so crucial to her condition.

Furthermore, we received contradictory instructions from the telephone support, the emergency veterinarian, and the staff working in the morning, without any satisfactory explanations.

The situation with the cytology was particularly serious: the hospital itself stated that the samples had already been scanned and sent to the pathologist. However, they refused to provide us with those digital images for a second evaluation and only gave us the physical slides.

We weren't asking for new tests or an expedited diagnosis, but rather access to files that, according to them, already existed. We had to submit written requests to obtain them.

We have reported these events to the Official College of Veterinarians of Madrid for their ethical review.

Our complaint is not about the lack of an immediate diagnosis, but about the treatment we received, the contradictions, and the obstacles we faced in accessing the tests for a dog with worrying symptoms.

A profoundly negative experience. We have lost confidence in this hospital.

This is an amazing and exceptional veterinary hospital! We were vacationing in Madrid when our shih tzu suffered 2 herniated disks in her spine. The veterinary team here,  lead by an amazing and dedicated neuro-surgeon, Dr Fernando, operated her. Within a few days she was pain free and mostly walking. We had great and loving support after the surgery from the neuro surgeon and his vet team, and from Miriam, a great fisio therapist, who worked with our doggie thoroughly, lovingly and so competently. The front desk team was also amazing and so responsive. Today,  3 weeks out of surgery,  our doggie is pain free, happy, and walking. We continue fisio therapy. We are most grateful for the Retiro team! We were in the best care! We are grateful.
The person who answers the phone is surprisingly unfriendly.

They are excellent. Quick diagnosis and they work 24 hours a day. Don't hesitate to take your pet there; I promise they'll make you feel better. Sara, the ophthalmologist, was very helpful and treated Capitán with all the love in the world, despite my dog's bad temper. I'm truly grateful.

I usually go to this vet when my dog ​​has a problem, and it's really good. It's 24 hours and conveniently located.

The reception staff are friendly, and the vets are excellent. I highly recommend it.
Excellent treatment and service, thank you for everything.

The law states that potentially dangerous dogs (PPP) must be muzzled and on a 1.5-meter leash in public places. This veterinarian allows PPP dogs to enter the waiting room without a muzzle, where everyone else is with their pets. I felt very uncomfortable having to tell someone with their pit bull to keep it by their side and not let it bother my dog, who was waiting peacefully and was sick! My dog ​​shouldn't be bothered by anyone, much less have its safety endangered. The law applies to everyone, and if a veterinary clinic breaks it, what other harm can it do?

Edited in response to the veterinarian's reply.


1. The requirement for a muzzle and leash exists and does not depend on whether the dog is "balanced."

Royal Decree 287/2002, which develops the regulations on potentially dangerous dogs, establishes in articles 8.2 and 8.3 that potentially dangerous dogs (PPPs), in public places and spaces, must wear the following:

* a suitable muzzle, and
* a non-extendable chain or leash of less than 2 meters.

It does not establish an exception for the owner considering the dog to be calm, well-behaved, or balanced.

Furthermore, Law 50/1999 also establishes that a leash/chain and muzzle are mandatory for the presence and movement of potentially dangerous dogs in public spaces.

Thank you for your response.

I understand that the obligation for the owner to properly restrain their dog falls to the person responsible for the animal. However, my comment did not refer to who has this obligation, but rather to the situation permitted within your waiting room.

In this regard, I have consulted the applicable regulations in Madrid, and the City Council itself expressly states that potentially dangerous dogs, when in public or private spaces for common use, must be under the control of a responsible person and, in the case of dogs, must wear a suitable muzzle and be on a leash of less than two meters.

Therefore, I understand that the fact that your center is a private establishment does not mean that this obligation disappears in a waiting room shared by different clients and animals.

Likewise, the fact that a dog is considered "balanced and well-behaved" does not seem to constitute an exception to the specific muzzle requirement established for potentially dangerous dogs.

My question, therefore, is very specific: what regulation allows a dog considered a potentially dangerous dog to remain in your waiting room without the muzzle required by law?

I do not question that the initial responsibility lies with the owner. What I question is why the center allows this situation to occur in a waiting room shared with other animals, some of whom are sick or especially vulnerable.
Forever grateful for the way they treated Maya. Excellent service and attention.

A few years ago, I was here studying, thinking it would be a good place.

I was horrified to discover that, far from being animal lovers, they allowed someone to practice as a veterinarian who, on more than one occasion, mistreated dogs right in front of me. Having zero patience, if a dog didn't lie down or position itself on the examination table in the hospitalization area the way he wanted, he would yell at it and forcefully push it down. He would also slam the door of another dog's cage and yell at it to be quiet.

I couldn't bear to endure that situation any longer, so I immediately requested a transfer to another center. I waited a while for fear it would affect my studies, but I couldn't stay silent any longer. If that veterinarian is still working here, which is highly likely since no one seemed to mind his behavior, I strongly advise you not to bring your animals here.

Hello, We regret that your experience at the hospital was not satisfactory. However, we have not been able to identify any visit or record associated with your name in our database, nor do we have any comments that would allow us to understand the reason for this rating.

If you would like to discuss your experience with us, please do so through our usual communication channels. This way, we can understand what happened and, if necessary, review it with the team to provide you with the best possible service.

Best regards.

The care Susito received was exceptional. The treatment was wonderful for both him and me; they called me twice a day during his three-day stay, which was also over the weekend, to explain how he was recovering from the effects of his fall and the surgery he had to undergo.

It's true that these services aren't cheap, but I had peace of mind knowing he was in good hands (although I know he's a very sweet kitten and very easy to love :) ) and I must say his recovery has been miraculous.
Excellent care, including checkups, emergency care, and the recent abdominal surgery.
We visited with our cockatiel and Iris's service was fabulous. She provided us with all the information we needed, treated our little one so well, and answered all our questions. Highly recommended.

A few weeks ago, I took my dog ​​to this clinic because there was no way to diagnose his digestive problem in my town. Antonio was the vet who saw us, and I couldn't be happier. He immediately put us at ease, ran some tests, explained everything, and gave us a diet and treatment plan. My dog ​​soon started to improve and feel much better. I have to thank this man because I literally feel like he saved my pet. 100% recommended.
Pio received excellent care

We took my dog ​​(medium-sized, 11 years old) to the emergency vet. The first thing they told us was that she was in serious condition and needed to be hospitalized for about 48 hours to stabilize an abnormality that appeared in her blood tests (associated with kidney failure). They said it was a common situation that would resolve with hospitalization.

After 24 hours, they told us that the results had improved. We went to see her, and to our surprise, she looked much worse than when we first saw her (since she was otherwise normal in both appearance and temperament). She didn't even recognize us. After much insistence, they told us it "might" be the medication. We were very disappointed, but since the results had improved slightly, they said she had to stay another night, and we agreed, for her sake.

The next day they said they would call us to update us on the dog's condition, but we had to keep trying all day to speak to a veterinarian. He finally called, but didn't give us the results of the latest tests and said he would call back in a few hours to discuss her condition. This call never came, showing a complete lack of concern for our situation. Finally, we managed to get the results from the receptionist, and her condition had worsened again. No veterinarian offered any explanation or even spoke to us. Seeing that nothing they were doing was helping, we decided to take her home. Even though we called ahead to let them know we were coming so they could prepare her for us, they refused to give her back without speaking to the veterinarian, even though he wasn't the one who had been treating her. After much insistence that all we wanted was our dog back because we were going to another clinic (while this doctor was simply selling food to another couple with their dog, showing no interest in us whatsoever), after arguing and even pleading with a random veterinarian, he finally took pity on our situation and took our dog with us.
We left extremely upset, not only because of the animal's condition but also because of the treatment we received at a clinic that is supposed to be good, as reflected in its fees. We absolutely do not recommend this clinic if your animals have a very serious problem, as they justify it by saying there are no more options for the animal while charging exorbitant fees for hospitalizations and tests. They should be honest from the beginning, tell us the true condition of our pet, and let the owners decide how to proceed. Everything mentioned here reflects their lack of empathy for animals and for those of us who love them.

No matter what the clinic says, look for other places with more heart; my dog ​​died a few days later.
Great, thanks 😊 …

We want to thank the ENTIRE team, especially our vet David, who are fabulous. We also want to thank Maria from the gastroenterology department, who is fabulous like all of them for her patience and kindness. We also don't want to forget the reception staff, especially Andrea; you are wonderful!! Greetings, Roy and Cooper.

After spending an entire weekday morning waiting for some simple tests, they had the nerve to charge us for emergency service. To make matters worse, the tests were incorrect, at a crucial time for our cat Alba. I DO NOT RECOMMEND them. There's little empathy and little professionalism. It's just a business, nothing more! And please stop "hiding" the reviews you don't like!
Terrible service. Disorganized, generally uninterested, very unprofessional. Extremely low medical level… and endless waits.
So far, the best in terms of attentive, caring with cats 🐱 and dogs 🐕, and punctual. Thank you, Sara, for taking such good care of Nala.

It's been almost a year since we met Antonio Varo when we went to the Retiro Veterinary Hospital for my dog's pyometra. She underwent emergency surgery, which was complicated by another problem that appeared around the same time but was very difficult to detect: a deep abscess that made us fear for her life.

Thanks to Antonio's intervention, the problem was identified and resolved very successfully. Since then, our dog has had other significant health issues, and Antonio's intervention has been crucial in resolving them.

I also want to thank María Orallo, the first veterinarian we saw at the Hospital, whose prescriptions and advice have ensured our dogs' digestive health is excellent.
So, we want to congratulate Antonio, María, and, of course, all the wonderful staff at Retiro Hospital for their professionalism and empathy.

It's such a relief to have found a place we can go with complete confidence for our dogs' care whenever they need it. Thank you so much Antonio, María and Retiro Veterinary Hospital!

I don't have enough stars to rate this hospital.

I've been taking my dogs here for many years for various reasons, and the treatment, care, and professionalism have always been outstanding.

This last visit was for surgery to remove a growth on my dog's eyelid, performed by Sara, an ophthalmologist. Besides congratulating her personally, I'm doing so here as well.

You can't even tell he's been in surgery. The care and dedication from both her and the rest of the team are incredible.

Either of my dogs goes there happy knowing how well they're treated and how loved they are.

The only clinic I trust completely.
Excellent service. Punctual and efficient.

I went because my dog ​​had eaten something at the park that looked like a bone, and they took wonderful care of him. It was all quite quick; they took an x-ray and finally made him vomit. In the end, everything turned out fine. A huge thank you to the team who looked after my dog! 🫶 …

I took my dog ​​to the emergency vet because something was stuck in her eye. First, the receptionist showed absolutely no empathy for an emergency and couldn't tell me how long I'd have to wait. Then, a vet, without even examining her, wanted to operate and who knows what else. I went to another vet, and they simply removed a flower with resin stuck in her fur with saline solution; they didn't even touch her eye. Completely unprofessional.

Dr. Iris is a wonderful veterinarian with a huge heart.

I recently took my cats, León and Melocotón, to the Retiro Veterinary Hospital, and Dr. Iris treated them. I can't thank her enough.
Her love and sensitivity towards animals are immediately apparent. She treated my kittens with such gentleness and patience that I felt completely safe and at ease.

And to that warmth, she adds impeccable professionalism: clear, attentive, and very confident in everything she does.

I left knowing that León and Melocotón are in the best hands.

Thank you, Iris, for taking such good care of them!

And thank you to the Retiro Veterinary Hospital for having professionals like Iris!
Delighted from the very first moment. From the reception staff to the veterinarian.
Open 24 hours a day, every day. They take great care of your pets and provide excellent medical attention.

Excellent clinic. Wonderful and professional treatment and care.
Very good professionals and a very caring and professional approach, especially from the veterinarian Iris, who is treating Pelayo. She is a great professional and has excellent personal touch.
Excellent, very good.

I was seen by a vet named David. He examined the kittens I'd found in the street and, to begin with, said they were a month and a half old when they're not even a month old. Thank goodness he weighed them, because he didn't even take their temperature… He told me they looked fine, even though the mother cat was in terrible condition. He also said the skin bumps were likely papillomavirus, which is extremely rare in cats. It turns out they have ear fungus, and I didn't find that out from this vet either. I had to go to another clinic where they received the proper diagnosis. It also turns out the mother cat has conjunctivitis; again, I only found that out from the other vet… Disappointing, to say the least, not just because of the €40 they charged me for basically telling me the sex and weight of each kitten, but because of the incompetence that often leads to death, distress, and suffering for animals.
A disgrace.

We are delighted with this hospital! Luckily, our dog had never been sick in five years.
Our husky, named Arnold, became very ill with an intestinal and liver infection. Since he had never been sick before, we were very anxious about having to admit him... but now we owe them everything and can only be eternally grateful. The rehydration process and medication were perfect. The diagnosis was correct from the beginning, and we highly recommend this hospital due to their professionalism and honesty (they never tried to sell us more than Arnold truly needed). The care we received from Arnold was impeccable. He was hospitalized for two days, and we were able to visit him and take him for walks. We observed that the dog was happy and very well cared for. We were particularly impressed with his cleanliness, as his stools were both numerous and not very healthy.
We also want to give special mention to the veterinarians Ricardo and Daniel. Ricardo made the correct diagnosis, and Daniel oversaw the final stages of Arnold's recovery. Our little dog is now happily home with us, he's regained all the weight he lost, and we'll continue with the prescribed treatment.

We hope we won't have to see them for a long time, but we would definitely go back to them if we had any health problems. Arnold was happy and you could see how he approached all the hospital staff.

The telephone service was quite disappointing. I called several times today to ask a question, and on numerous occasions, they picked up the phone and hung up immediately without even answering my question.

After several attempts, I finally got through. I explained my situation politely, and the response I received was very brief, curt, and quite rude, with little interest shown in helping or explaining the situation.

I understand that they might be busy or have a high volume of calls, but I think there's a difference between being overwhelmed and treating someone this way when they're trying to resolve a question about their pet. At the very least, I expected more professional service and a bit more empathy.

It's a shame, because telephone service is also part of the overall experience, and in this case, it was very negative.

Bad experience with telephone service.
I called to ask if it was possible to have my dog's nails trimmed under some kind of light sedation, as it's practically impossible to trim them myself because she won't let anyone touch her. My intention was to have it done at a veterinary clinic precisely so it would be done safely, avoiding a bad experience at a groomer's and ensuring her nails were treated properly.
After eight calls and about 20 minutes of waiting, the receptionist finally answered. Her response, delivered in a rather unpleasant tone, was to go to a groomer's, as they didn't do that there and couldn't do anything about it.
I completely understand that a clinic might not offer that service or that there might be certain conditions for doing so, but I believe there are much more professional and pleasant ways to assist and guide a client, especially when it's a question related to a pet's well-being and health. I'm left with a very negative feeling after this call. I'll try contacting the clinic another day, hoping for a different approach and, above all, someone who can properly advise me on the best option for my dog.

Since it's my clinic.
A month ago I brought a pigeon to her, and thanks to Iris, who taught me how to care for it, I was able to release it this week. You clearly love your job. Thank you for all your help.

I tried calling, but my call gets disconnected every time. I still can't even reach this veterinarian by phone. No one answers. And WhatsApp says they don't have it. I don't know how to contact them when they don't reply. It's a real shame.

I take my dog ​​there and they take excellent care of her. Whenever she's needed to be hospitalized, they've always given a perfect diagnosis and treatment, knowing exactly what was wrong with her. They have many tests available at the center, so you don't have to go anywhere else. The staff is wonderful, from reception to the veterinarians and the hospital itself—everything is perfect. I highly recommend them; they care for pets with professionalism and lots of love.

I think all of us who have any kind of pet are afraid to take them anywhere and always have the uncertainty of whether they'll be treated well, whether they'll receive the same affection we show our own animals, and so on. A month ago, my 10-year-old dog, Maya, started having seizures and exhibiting many strange changes, such as changes in her behavior, always wanting to sleep, and refusing to eat. One day she started drooling a lot and became restless. The next day we took her to another vet, and they charged us €500 just for an examination. About a week later, she started having seizures again, and a friend of my mother recommended this hospital. We went, and they diagnosed her with epilepsy. We were very worried. She was hospitalized for two days, and obviously, like any patient, we had to wait for progress. To this day, we are grateful to this hospital and to Dr. Ricardo, who was handling Maya's case. Now she greets us and has started playing with us, something she never did before. I recommend this place 1000%. I know that, unlike other places, this one would never try to take advantage of you and squeeze money out of you unnecessarily. Thanks to them, Maya is back to her old self, and although she's still on medication, I'm happy to know I can have her in my life for a while longer.

I'm not commenting on the care my pet receives, but I live 50 km away and I've called more than 6 times, only to be put on hold and then they hang up on me when it's finally my turn. I have an emergency, and if I go there and they refuse to help me, what am I supposed to do? Raise a ruckus?

I don’t even know where to start to express my gratitude… our dog is alive thanks to the professionalism of the whole team! She arrived in a critical state transferred from another veterinary hospital that couldn’t operate on her - and the team was ready to take her in and operate immediately.  Pablo the surgeon is a superhero and deserves a statue ! The receptionist was understanding and gentle and pacient with us - my hands were shaking so much I couldn’t even sign the form. Thank you 🙏 thank you for everything!

Curro tore his cruciate ligament at the end of March. We brought him here, and they reassured us from the very beginning. After the necessary tests, he had surgery in April, and everything went perfectly. Today he was given his final discharge, although he hadn't been limping for months. The treatment and professionalism were wonderful. Thank you, Pablo, and the whole team.

Curro, Dani, and Ruth
Very friendly and good service. They were kind to my dog.

I want to express my deepest gratitude to Pablo, a specialist in brachycephalic dogs, for the excellent work he did. My dog ​​underwent soft palate surgery and pharyngeal blockage correction, a procedure that terrified me, but everything went perfectly.

From the very first moment, Pablo exuded professionalism, confidence, and a friendly approach, explaining each step clearly and answering all my questions. The operation was a success, and her recovery is going very well, which gives me enormous peace of mind. I wholeheartedly recommend him to anyone who owns a brachycephalic dog and needs a true specialist.
The best care, professionalism, very kind, and everything was so fast! Thank you for taking such good care of my baby! From the receptionists to the last doctor we spoke to, everyone was fantastic!

The center uses a name that doesn't correspond to any existing company and conceals the fact that they are called Petsalud/Vetpartners, which is the entity responsible for civil and criminal liability.

All responsibility for their practices should fall on their technical director, Dr. Rafael Pérez Marcos, Col. 5410, who reinforces the corporate policies of this animal slaughterhouse.

They belong to Vetpartners UK, which in turn belongs to BC Partners, and they do the same things in Spain for which they have been convicted in the UK.

They hide their true identity, don't offer quotes or information about the treatments they will provide beforehand, don't keep a record of pets' medical histories and refuse to provide them when requested, discriminate against cases they deem unprofitable, ignore pets' previous medical histories, lie in their responses to negative reviews, and kill hundreds of animals.

At the end of January, I went there because Soma was lame. They took x-rays and told me they couldn't see anything and refused to do anything else. I took him for more tests, but he was still limping, so I took him back twelve more times. On the thirteenth visit, they told me he had cancer, after two and a half months had passed.

I don't mean to say that cancer is easy to cure, but an early diagnosis, ordering a CT scan when they don't see anything on the x-rays, and more love for animals and less focus on the financial aspect for their owners would have helped. It's possible that Soma could have been saved, because there was a chance, if they hadn't allowed the metastasis to progress due to their malpractice.

Soma has died, and I join the negative opinions that consider Retiro Veterinary Hospital an animal slaughterhouse, not a service that cares for pets.

Hello: We regret your feedback.
We haven't been able to locate your identity in our system, nor do we have any further information in your comment.
Therefore, we invite you to contact us with more details so we can address your case.
Regards.
Everything was perfect, excellent service, Sara was outstanding
Highly recommended. Excellent service.

I do not recommend this veterinary hospital. Veterinarian David saw my dog, Mila, and diagnosed otitis without detecting that she actually had foxtails in her ear. He only prescribed ear irrigation, which caused her to suffer unnecessarily. Furthermore, he gave me incorrect information about the procedure for obtaining a sample and the diagnosis. My experience was very disappointing, and I hope my review will serve as a warning to other pet owners to be vigilant and seek a second opinion when necessary.

A terrible experience. Absolutely arrogant treatment, misdiagnosis, and a fatal outcome. I wouldn't wish this place on my worst enemy. Sadly, my case is beyond repair, but I wish I could warn everyone not to go here under any circumstances. Seek other professional opinions, where they actually listen to the human being and care about the animal before the money.

Hello Daniel, we are sorry to hear about your feedback.
We haven't been able to locate your identity in our system, and we don't have any further information in your comment.
Therefore, we invite you to contact us with more details so we can address your case.
Regards.

My experience at this clinic was very disappointing. I went with my pet and they charged me €89 for a 10-minute consultation. Since the veterinarian indicated that the case wasn't within their area of ​​expertise, they referred me to the dermatologist at the same clinic for the following day.

To my surprise, because it was an internal referral and I hadn't been informed beforehand, they charged me another €89 for the specialist's consultation. At no point was I notified that I would have to pay for a second, full consultation, which I consider opaque and very unfriendly to the customer.

I understand that a specialist has their fees, but I also believe that a clinic should clearly inform you of all costs before providing the service, especially when the referral is between professionals within the same establishment.

I felt misinformed and with the impression that billing takes precedence over customer service. Based on my experience, I will not return to this clinic, nor would I recommend it. No check-up, no service—they're scammers.
I want to thank the hospital in general and Antonio, my dog ​​Ares's veterinarian, in particular for their dedication and commitment shown at every appointment. You finally did it!
We are so grateful for the excellent care; they are truly great professionals! My dog ​​arrived very sick, but thanks to God and them, he has been able to pull through.
Excellent service and empathy at reception, especially with my pet. The same goes for all the other staff. Thank you!
The veterinarians and assistants are very professional, special mention to Pablo the traumatologist who followed up with my pet until he was fully recovered.

I took my dog ​​for a checkup, using my Asisa insurance, which they already knew because she was on file. The vet decided to do some tests. The policy includes a complete blood count (CBC), but they never told me which parameters they were going to check. I mention this because they charge €24.40 per parameter, not including the CBC itself, and the description is just basic biochemistry. It's nothing special, just standard parameters, no test for Leishmania or anything like that. In total, €170.80 for a basic analysis plus €21.78 for the CBC, which my insurance covered.
Of course, I've filed a complaint and am awaiting a resolution. My advice is that before they take your pet out for tests, make sure you know exactly what they're going to do and how much they'll cost, especially if you're using health insurance. This is a common practice; I'm neither the first nor the last.

Edit regarding your response: I never said the veterinarian didn't perform the relevant tests or those he deemed necessary. That's a matter of medical judgment, and if he informs me and I agree, I have no objection. You're being overly focused on the insurance issue, but I'd say the same thing if I were without any insurance. You're obligated to inform me of the cost and the exact tests (including the parameters to be measured). Imagine if the doctor decides that 12 parameters need to be checked. The least you can do is inform me, especially since I might not be able to afford it. It's a matter of transparency and Article 60 of the Consumer Protection Act.
I say I'm not the first because on the two occasions I've been there, many people were surprised that some tests weren't covered by insurance and that your prices are so high. I was sitting next to reception, which is why I mention it. But anyway, you know you work with health insurance companies and who has which insurance and what it does or doesn't cover. Claiming ignorance of the policy doesn't make much sense when you apply the discounts and issue an invoice.
It's a disgrace! I waited 1 hour and 30 minutes only to be left stranded without being able to visit my dog. I'm speechless. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone.

I'll be objective: we arrived with an emergency (visible blood in his urine, tremors, clearly deteriorating, labored breathing, and constant whimpering). We had called before going and were told to come immediately. As soon as we arrived, they told us we had to wait 20 minutes or more for the doctors to finish their rounds. I explained that we were there in an emergency, but they didn't say anything and invited us to sit down. Half an hour passed, and there were already four of us waiting. They spoke to all of us and said that the doctors wouldn't be able to see anyone for at least another two hours, and that it might be even longer. We had to go to another hospital where they saw us as soon as we arrived because, although the doctors were busy, they understood that this situation was critical and urgent. Elvis is still hospitalized and in delicate condition. I'll spare you some of my personal opinions; all I'll say is that these kinds of places clearly operate without empathy or love for animals. It's just a business.

The best vet I've ever been to, and I've been involved with animals and animal rescue organizations for years.

David and Antonio are amazing, and Ari is wonderful. My dogs are in good hands, and I feel calm and grateful.

I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone. The customer service is awful. Very good experience and very good professionals.

My experience with the Retiro Veterinary Clinic has been complex and, in some ways, disappointing, although I try to evaluate it objectively.

On the one hand, it is a well-equipped and reputable center in Madrid, which initially inspires confidence. However, my specific clinical experience with several of my cats has been inconsistent.

In one case, during a sterilization, a serious complication arose involving the spleen, which subsequently required revision surgery and raised doubts for me about the surgical management and the preoperative assessment.

In another case, faced with a respiratory problem, invasive tests such as bronchoalveolar lavage were considered too early, at a high cost. Ultimately, the condition improved favorably with antibiotic treatment (doxycycline), without the need for these tests, which makes me question whether the initial approach was proportionate or excessively interventionist.

My overall impression is that there's a tendency to recommend advanced tests too early, without first exhausting more conservative diagnostic and therapeutic options. This can have a significant financial impact on families, especially those with multiple pets.

I've also noticed a lack of individualized clinical judgment and better communication in decision-making, taking into account not only what's technically possible, but also what's clinically necessary in each case.

That said, I believe that every case and every professional can be different, even within the same clinic, but my personal experience leads me to recommend that other owners seek second opinions and carefully consider the indications before undergoing invasive or expensive tests.

This opinion is based on my direct experience as the owner of several cats with complex health conditions.
